title: So You Think You Can Rule the World?
department: Political Economy, Game Theory & Venture Strategy
tagline: An Intensive 6-Book Curriculum in Power, Game Theory, Monopolies, and Institutional Dominance
description: Six masterwork 30-minute book summaries exploring the hidden game-theoretic laws governing geopolitics, Silicon Valley monopolies, corporate boardrooms, and institutional decay.
syllabusTakeaway: Master the structural forces of coordination failures, competitive moats, coalition survival, and moral counterweights in modern systems of power.

books.title: Meditations on Moloch
books.author: Scott Alexander (Slate Star Codex)
books.keyTakeaway: How hyper-competition forces rational agents to sacrifice every human value for a slight competitive edge.

books.title: The Tragedy of the Commons & Governing the Commons
books.author: Garrett Hardin & Elinor Ostrom
books.primaryText: "The Tragedy of the Commons" by Garrett Hardin & Governing the Commons by Elinor Ostrom
books.keyTakeaway: Why shared resources collapse under individual self-interest and how private or institutional rules enforce order.

books.title: The Evolution of Cooperation
books.author: Robert Axelrod
books.primaryText: The Evolution of Cooperation by Robert Axelrod
books.keyTakeaway: How iterated Prisoner's Dilemmas work in the real world, and when "Tit-for-Tat" or defection wins.

books.title: Zero to One
books.author: Peter Thiel (Stanford CS183)
books.primaryText: Zero to One by Peter Thiel (Stanford CS183)
books.keyTakeaway: Why competition destroys profits and how founders build monopolies to escape multipolar traps.

books.title: The Dictator's Handbook
books.author: Bruce Bueno de Mesquita & Alastair Smith
books.primaryText: The Dictator's Handbook by Bruce Bueno de Mesquita & Alastair Smith
books.keyTakeaway: Selectorate theory: why leaders and CEOs act the way they do based purely on keeping their "winning coalition" paid.

books.title: How to Rule the World: An Education in Power at Stanford University
books.author: Theo Baker (2026)
books.primaryText: How to Rule the World: An Education in Power at Stanford University by Theo Baker (2026)
books.keyTakeaway: The investigative account of the "Rule" seminar, Stanford's VC shadow networks, and the ethical fallout of this mindset.
